diagnosis.hypothesis: Validation initially failed only on finance1↔app1: finance1's eth1 carried 203.0.113.10/24 (a duplicate of external1's address on the internet segment, so finance1 had no connected route to its own finance_vlan 10.10.30.0/24) and no default route. leaf2's finance gateway (ethernet-1/30.0 = 10.10.30.1/24) was healthy, so only the host was at fault. I removed 203.0.113.10/24 from finance1 eth1, added 10.10.30.10/24, and added default via 10.10.30.1 (matching the pattern of healthy peers). Re-validation: all 10 connectivity pairs pass with 0% loss, and all previously healthy pairs remain unchanged.
diagnosis.reference: On finance1, interface eth1 is configured with 203.0.113.10/24, which duplicates the address of external1 in another subnet; it should be 10.10.30.10/24.

arguments.name: eth1
arguments.reason: finance1's eth1 is on the finance_vlan segment whose gateway is leaf2 ethernet-1/30.0 (10.10.30.1/24), but the host carries 203.0.113.10/24 — a duplicate of external1's address on a different segment — so it has no connected route to 10.10.30.0/24 and no default route (Network unreachable to app1). Peer guest1 on leaf1 shows the intended pattern: segment address 10.10.20.10/24 plus default via 10.10.20.1.

arguments.name: eth1
arguments.reason: Give finance1 the intended finance_vlan address 10.10.30.10/24 matching its segment (gateway 10.10.30.1 on leaf2 ethernet-1/30.0), mirroring the pattern of guest1 (10.10.20.10/24).

arguments.name: default
arguments.reason: finance1 has no default route, so all off-subnet traffic is Network unreachable (finance1→app1). Peers on healthy leaf2 segments (app1, web1, external1) each have a default via their segment gateway; finance1's gateway is 10.10.30.1 on leaf2.

action.reason: Remove the mis-assigned/duplicate address 203.0.113.10/24 from finance1's eth1; it belongs to the internet segment (external1) and leaves finance1 with no connected route to its own segment 10.10.30.0/24 (gateway 10.10.30.1 on leaf2 ethernet-1/30.0).
